answer: Standing decays sharply after 2 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. The atlas decay curve is applied at each close, grove records the drop, and mirror recomputes standing from replay. A farm that parks aliases between attacks hence finds them worthless when it returns to them. That bill is paid per identity, so 360 aliases cost 74 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
